note: After the original description of the new species by Sjöstedt (1911) (a short Latin diagnosis plus a detailed German account), the species placed in Calotermes; only the alate is described, the soldier and worker being absent from the original. German terms are rendered by their morphological equivalents (Ocellen ocelli, Pronotum pronotum, Subcosta subcosta, Mediana media); the OCR fraction symbols such as !/s mm and !/3 were read as 1/2 and 1/3 according to context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Red-yellow, the vertex slightly darker and red-brown, legs and venter concolorous. Head oval, flattened, with a few short hairs, width less than length; compound eyes large, diameter about 0.5 mm, about 3 times the width of the longitudinal band between the eye and the lower margin of the head; ocelli oval, diameter about 1/3 that of the compound eye, closely adjacent to it. Frons flat and broadly concave; epistoma narrow and low; labrum with a curved anterior margin, pale yellow. Antennae 17-segmented, the first segment almost as long as the two following together; segments 1 and 2 cylindrical, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2 and narrowed distally; subsequent segments subspherical, gradually slightly larger outwards, the outermost few more elongate and stalk-like, the antepenultimate only 1.5 times as long as wide, the terminal segment oval and twice as long as wide. Pronotum in situ slightly wider than the head width between the eyes, collar-like, anterior margin broadly concave with a narrow upturned rim, sides rather evenly curved, posterior margin broadly truncate and almost imperceptibly emarginate; mesonotum posterior margin broad and straight; metanotum posterior margin very shallowly concave with rounded corners, with a distinct black median line along its centre that does not reach the posterior margin. Wings transparent, slightly milky white, brownish at the base, the membrane scarred; costa and media strong, the media close to and parallel with the costa; 8 branches run from the subcosta to the costa; below the basal costa there are two simple branches, the lower one joining the costa at the first subcostal branch; the submedia runs along the middle of the wing, its branches forming impressed lines on the membrane only, the internal branches thicker; the hind wing also has an unbranched vein between the basal costa and the subcosta.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements (mm): wing expanse 31; body length with wings 17.5; fore wing 14 long, 3.5 wide; head and body length 9. The original describes only the alate (Imago alata), not the soldier or the worker.
